# Binding instructions

The `.binding` stack holds keyed bindings: an int key and any item. The topmost binding with a key is that variable's current value, and older ones below it are shadowed, so each variable is a stack of its own. The inputs are bound to keys 0, 1, 2, … at load, and fresh keys follow them. Instructions that make or look up bindings use the verb *ref*.

## Operations

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bindingEq` |  | `binding` (read), `binding` (read) | `bool` |
| `bindingFromCode` |  | `code` | `binding` or `error`; may refuse |
| `bindingQuote` |  | `binding` | `code` |
| `bindingRekey` |  | `binding`, `int` | `binding` |

## Control

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refScope` |  | `int`, `code` | the rest of the program |

## Rearranging the stack

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refUnbind` |  | `int` (read) | `binding`, rearranged; may refuse |

## The stack's own instructions

Every stack has the same family for copying, deleting, reordering and measuring its items; see <doc:StackInstructions>. On `.binding` they are `bindingDeepDup`, `bindingDeleteAtDepth`, `bindingDup`, `bindingDupItems`, `bindingDupTimes`, `bindingFlush`, `bindingPop`, `bindingPopItems`, `bindingRot`, `bindingShove`, `bindingStackDepth`, `bindingStackIsEmpty`, `bindingSwap`, `bindingYank`, `bindingYankDup`.
